subject.title: [Feature]: models.providers.*.enabled flag to disable providers without removing config

question: Should OpenClaw add a provider-level `models.providers.<provider>.enabled` config contract that disables routing while preserving the provider config block?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible and useful, but the requested fix adds a persistent config option and changes provider-routing behavior across compatibility-sensitive surfaces.

options.title: Approve bounded contract
options.body: Implement the flag across schema, models.json planning, configured catalogs, fallback resolution, and `models status`, with default-enabled compatibility and focused tests.

options.title: Decline new config surface
options.body: Keep the current workaround of removing or editing provider blocks and avoid adding another persistent provider toggle.

options.title: Defer for routing design
options.body: Leave the issue open until maintainers decide broader provider disable, status, auth, and probe semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded contract
recommendation.body: Implement the flag across schema, models.json planning, configured catalogs, fallback resolution, and `models status`, with default-enabled compatibility and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest combined signal from prior issue review and recent model/config architecture history.
